name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard

controls.title: Restrict Network Communications to Approved Services, Protocols and Ports
controls.intent: Ensure that only explicitly authorised network services, protocols and ports are permitted, reducing unnecessary attack surface and preventing unauthorised communications.
controls.summary: Only services, protocols and ports with a documented business need should be reachable. Unexpected reachable services or ports indicate ineffective enforcement of network security controls.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA directly verifies whether observed network reachability matches the authorised communication policy defined in the segmentation model.
assessment_notes: A successful connection to a service or port that is not authorised by policy constitutes objective evidence that network security controls are not enforcing the intended restrictions.
limitations: Cannot determine whether the service was formally approved or documented.

controls.title: Verify the Continued Effectiveness of Network Security Controls
controls.intent: Ensure that network security controls continue to enforce only authorised communications and remain aligned with the intended security policy.
controls.summary: Unexpected connectivity may indicate that network security controls are no longer enforcing the intended policy and should be reviewed.
controls.nssa_relevance: Every NSSA finding represents technical evidence that the observed network behaviour differs from the expected segmentation policy.
assessment_notes: NSSA cannot determine whether periodic reviews are performed, but can provide objective evidence that network security controls are not behaving as intended.
limitations: Does not assess organisational review processes or change management activities.

controls.title: Restrict Network Access To and From the Cardholder Data Environment
controls.intent: Ensure that only explicitly authorised inbound and outbound communications are permitted between the CDE and other network segments.
controls.summary: All communications entering or leaving the CDE should be explicitly authorised. Unexpected connectivity indicates ineffective segmentation enforcement.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA directly validates whether observed connectivity towards or from protected assets matches the authorised segmentation policy.
assessment_notes: A single successful unauthorised connection entering or leaving the CDE is sufficient evidence that network isolation is not fully enforced.
limitations: Does not assess packet inspection, application-layer filtering or encrypted traffic inspection.

controls.title: Restrict Inbound Communications from Untrusted Networks
controls.intent: Ensure that only authorised inbound communications and legitimate responses to established connections are permitted into trusted networks.
controls.summary: Inbound communications should be restricted to authorised services and legitimate responses to established communications.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA can verify whether prohibited inbound communications succeed but cannot determine whether stateful inspection mechanisms are correctly implemented.
expected_evidence: Unauthorised communication from an untrusted network
assessment_notes: NSSA validates the observable behaviour of the network rather than the implementation of stateful inspection.
limitations: Cannot determine whether traffic is allowed as part of an existing stateful session.

controls.title: Prevent Direct Network Access to Systems Storing Cardholder Data
controls.intent: Ensure that systems storing cardholder data are not directly reachable from untrusted networks.
controls.summary: Systems storing cardholder data should only be reachable through authorised network paths. Direct access from untrusted networks represents ineffective segmentation.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA directly verifies whether protected assets are reachable from prohibited network segments.
assessment_notes: Successful direct communication with protected systems constitutes objective evidence that network isolation has failed.
limitations: Assumes the protected assets are correctly identified in the policy model.

controls.title: Mitigate Risks from Devices Connected to Both Untrusted Networks and the CDE
controls.intent: Reduce the risk that devices connected to untrusted networks can be used as a bridge to access the CDE.
controls.summary: Devices capable of communicating with both untrusted networks and the CDE should not create unauthorised communication paths into protected environments.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA can identify unexpected reachability involving devices connected to multiple trust zones but cannot assess endpoint security controls.
assessment_notes: NSSA validates network exposure but cannot determine whether host-based protections, such as endpoint security controls, are present.
limitations: Does not assess endpoint hardening, EDR, personal firewalls or device posture.

controls.title: Isolate System Functions with Different Security Levels
controls.intent: Ensure that system functions requiring different levels of protection cannot communicate in ways that reduce the security of higher-trust functions.
security_goal: Prevent lower-trust components from reaching higher-trust assets
controls.summary: Functions with different security requirements should be isolated so that lower-security workloads cannot adversely affect more sensitive systems.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA can validate whether the intended network isolation between workloads of different trust levels is effectively enforced.
assessment_notes: Observed communication between components that should be isolated indicates that the intended separation is not effectively enforced.
limitations: Cannot determine whether isolation is implemented through virtualization, containers, operating system mechanisms or network controls.

controls.title: Limit Exposed Network Services to Those Required for Business
controls.intent: Reduce the attack surface by ensuring that only required network-accessible services are exposed.
controls.summary: Only network services that are required for business operation should be reachable. Unexpected exposed services increase the attack surface.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA can identify services that are reachable over the network but are not expected according to the declared segmentation policy.
expected_evidence: Network exposure not defined by policy
assessment_notes: NSSA evaluates externally observable network exposure rather than the internal software configuration of the host.
limitations: Cannot determine whether unnecessary services exist but are not network-accessible.

controls.title: Restrict Network Access According to Business Need
controls.intent: Ensure that only authorised systems are able to establish network communication with protected resources according to business need and least privilege principles.
controls.summary: Network communication should only be possible from systems that have an explicit business need to access the protected resource. Unexpected connectivity indicates excessive network access privileges.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA validates whether observed network reachability matches the authorised host-to-service relationships defined in the segmentation policy.
assessment_notes: The finding concerns network-level authorisation rather than user authentication or application permissions.
Observed communication from a host that is not explicitly authorised provides objective evidence that least-privilege network access is not being enforced.
limitations: Cannot determine user identities, application roles, RBAC, ABAC or operating-system permissions.
Cannot determine whether application-layer authorisation subsequently denied the request.

controls.title: Validate PCI DSS Scope Through Segmentation Verification
controls.intent: Ensure that the defined PCI DSS scope remains accurate by periodically validating that network segmentation controls continue to isolate the Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) from out-of-scope systems.
security_goal: Verify continued effectiveness of network segmentation
Detect scope expansion caused by segmentation failures
controls.summary: Network segmentation should continue to enforce the intended PCI DSS scope by preventing unauthorized communication between in-scope and out-of-scope environments. Unexpected reachability may indicate that the effective PCI DSS scope has changed.
controls.nssa_relevance: NSSA provides technical evidence supporting PCI DSS scope validation by verifying whether observed network connectivity matches the intended segmentation policy and whether the CDE remains properly isolated.
expected_evidence: Unauthorized network path crossing scope boundaries
assessment_notes: NSSA contributes evidence for the network segmentation portion of PCI DSS scope validation.
Unexpected reachability may indicate that systems previously considered out of scope have become effectively connected to the CDE.
limitations: Does not identify cardholder data locations.
Does not discover payment data flows.
Does not build or validate complete PCI DSS scope documentation.
Does not replace a full PCI DSS scoping exercise.
